narrative.overview:
The site is a workshop after dark: a near-black room, a bench of finished artifacts, and warm task lighting that falls only where someone is working. The darkness is not moody for its own sake — it is what makes the light legible. Coral, amber, and yellow behave like lamp filaments and solder points: small, hot, and never used as wallpaper.

Density is moderate and rhythmic. Each section opens the same way — a numbered label in warm type, a headline pinned to the left edge, a muted sub-line across the page — then fills the bench with a single kind of artifact: skill cards, a timeline, project entries, a contact panel. Nothing floats free of the ground.

Motion is the workshop's tell. Elements arrive as if placed rather than animated: a 30px rise on reveal, spring physics on tilt and press, a magnetic pull on the primary actions. It reads as confident handling, not spectacle. The one inconsistency in the room is the hero, which was repainted in violet and lime and never carried through to the rest of the page; it is recorded as an exception, not as the system.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with a subtle 60px grid and three radial warm glows
Warm ramp used as signal, never as fill area
One type family, hierarchy carried by size, weight, and negative tracking
Flat surfaces at rest; shadow reserved for things that float
Pills for controls, 18px cards for artifacts, 28px panel for the contact close

rules.name: The Workbench Rule
rules.body: Warm color marks an active thing — a label, a focus ring, a live control, a hover rule. If warm color is covering more than a small fraction of a viewport, it has become decoration and the design is wrong.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Coral, amber, and yellow are three intensities of one light, not three brand colors. Never introduce a fourth hue; the hero violet and lime are evidence of what happens when you do.

rules.name: The Single Voice Rule
rules.body: One family. If a new surface seems to need a second typeface, it needs a different weight or tracking instead.

rules.name: The Tight Head Rule
rules.body: Anything at 19px or larger gets negative tracking. Headlines at -0.03em, display at -0.035em. Untracked large type reads as unfinished.

rules.name: The Flat-Bench Rule
rules.body: A card that is not floating does not cast a shadow. If a surface needs to feel more important, raise its fill one step and strengthen its border — do not add a drop shadow.

dos: Do keep warm color on marks, labels, focus states, and small controls; measure it as a fraction of the viewport, not of the brand.
Do use the 90px / 70px section rhythm and the shared header pattern on any new section.
Do carry depth with a hairline and a one-step fill change.
Do put negative tracking on anything 19px or larger.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: reveals resolve instantly and Lenis smooth scroll is switched off.
Do test every new surface in Arabic RTL — the language switcher, contact email, and layout mirroring are already handled and must not regress.
donts: Don't introduce a fourth accent hue. Violet and lime exist only as the hero's documented drift.
Don't fill a card, section, or button with the warm ramp; the gradient belongs to hairlines, text, and the contact panel wash.
Don't add a drop shadow to a resting card.
Don't add a second typeface for "editorial" or "technical" flavor.
Don't mix radii — pills for controls, 18px cards, 28px panel, nothing in between.
Don't animate anything the visitor did not ask for on operate-style surfaces (form fields, nav); motion belongs to arrival and to pointer response.
